title: Pilot sync: model choices and rollback plan
next_steps: Redwood to share flattened perf spreadsheet comparing catalog models by EOD Thursday
Customer to confirm which two models to pin for canary by next Tuesday
SE to run KV-cache stress test and share logs
Schedule rollback drill with AtlasMetrics infra team next week
action_items: Priya Shah: run 50k token prefix KV-cache test, due 2025-04-18
Alex Moran: send pricing delta for dedicated vs hosted canary, due 2025-04-17
Elena Park: provide two representative prompt sets for regression tests, due 2025-04-16
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on narrowing model candidates and defining a concrete pinning and rollback strategy for the pilot. Reviewed recent perf and quality tradeoffs; agreed next steps for stress tests and pricing split for canary. Security and SRE asked for a rollback drill and additional audit log details.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-04-15 / 10:00 PT / Duration ~47m
Attendees: Alex Moran (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Diego Ramos (Redwood Platform), Morgan Lee (AtlasMetrics PM), Elena Park (AtlasMetrics ML), Jordan Smith (AtlasMetrics SRE), Samir Patel (AtlasMetrics Security)
Recording note: auto-transcript, medium quality, some mis-heard acronyms.

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. Agenda—quick perf recap, pick models for canary/pin, and outline rollback plan. Priya, you wanna start with the perf highlights?
[01:02] Priya: Yep, thanks Alex. We ran the week-over-week benchmarking across the catalog variants you gave us—two base candidates plus a quantized variant. Raw numbers: median p50 latency on the hosted endpoint for model A was ~82ms per token, model B ~68ms, quantized B (q4) jumped cost down 18% but latency was a hair higher at 72ms. Note: these are median single-request numbers; tail p95 was spikier on model A especially under 8k token contexts.
[02:18] Morgan: Sorry, when you say model A/B can you restate the family names? Our team labeled them differently.
[02:31] Priya: Right, apologies—model A is "Orchid-1.3" from the catalog; model B is "Cedar-2-legacy" recompiled with attention opt. The q4 is Cedar-2 q4-2.
[03:05] Elena: This matches what we saw in our offline evals—Cedar-2 gives better continuity for our summarization prompts, fewer hallucinations. Orchid sometimes hallucinates dates.
[03:45] Jordan: On infra impact, Cedar-2 had higher KV cache footprint in memory—about 12% more GPU RAM when we pinned long prefix. That means fewer concurrent sessions per pod.
[04:12] Diego: Right, that's the kernel selection tradeoff—Cedar's attention kernel uses more memory for the optimized kv store. We can tune batching but it affects latency.
[04:45] Samir: From security: are audit logs for model variants captured per request? We need an immutable trail when we switch versions.
[05:10] Alex: Yes, Redwood console captures model version in the request trace. We'll share a sample log.
[05:28] Morgan: Ok, goal for this week is to pick two models to pin: one primary and one fallback for canary. We also need rollback criteria.
[06:01] Priya: Suggestion: primary—Cedar-2 (non-quant) for quality, fallback—Cedar-2 q4 for cost/timeouts? Or Orchid-1.3 as an alternate fallback if Cedar variants hit capacity. The fallback must be compatible in API and tokenization.
[06:36] Elena: We prefer Cedar-2 non-quant for accuracy. For fallback I'd lean toward Orchid-1.3 because its memory footprint is smaller and it's cheaper to spin up. But recall Orchid had some hallucination issues—we'd need stricter monitoring.
[07:05] Jordan: If we choose Orchid as fallback, we need deterministic rollback windows and a canary traffic slice small enough to limit blast radius. We should automate rollback on QA metric drops.
[07:40] Priya: Agreed—Redwood supports automated fallback to a pinned model variant by policy: e.g., if p95 latency > 300ms or quality-regression > 5% on holdout prompts. But quality checks require your eval harness to push metrics back.
[08:12] Morgan: Elena, can your team instrument the eval harness to emit quality metrics to the webhook?
[08:20] Elena: Yes, we can. We'll send two sets of test prompts and expected outputs by tomorrow.
[08:30] Alex: Make a note—Elena to provide prompt sets by 2025-04-16.
[09:00] [timestamp gap: lost section due to muffled audio]
[10:12] Priya: We also ran KV-cache stress test in a simulated multi-tenant scenario. With Cedar pinned, cache hit ratio improved overall but eviction spikes happen around 6k token sequences. That led to transient latency bumps.
[11:00] Jordan: That eviction behavior is concerning—our customer flows often include long transcripts. What are our mitigation options?
[11:22] Diego: Options: increase per-session cache allocation which reduces concurrency; implement dynamic prefix trimming so we limit KV length for long chats; or use stateless mode with more frequent recompute which is higher cost.
[11:48] Morgan: What's the expected cost delta for increasing cache alloc?
[12:05] Alex: Rough numbers—alloc bump to avoid evictions reduces effective concurrency by ~15% which roughly scales to 12-18% monthly cost increase under our current pilot load. We'll quantify and send a spreadsheet.
[12:42] Priya: Also, note when we trigger fallback to q4 variant, tokenization differences changed the token counts by about 2-5% which slightly impacts per-token billing.
[13:05] Elena: Important for our budgeting—please include that in the cost sheet.
[13:18] Alex: Will do.
[13:40] Samir: Back to security and rollback: can we do a rollback drill next week? We need to validate SSO/permissions recovery, audit logs, and that KMS-wrapped keys are accessible after redeploy.
[14:05] Diego: We can schedule a rollback drill. Redwood private customers sometimes do a dry-run with their infra. For hosted, we can simulate by toggling traffic rules and verify logs.
[14:32] Morgan: Let's plan a drill with our SRE and Redwood SE next Wednesday.
[14:45] Alex: Noted—schedule for 2025-04-23 10am PT? I'll send a calendar invite.
[15:00] Priya: Quick note on model pinning semantics—Redwood lets you pin to a model version ID. We recommend pinning by immutable version rather than model family tag to ensure deterministic rollbacks. Also, pin both primary and fallback with explicit fallback policies.
[15:35] Elena: Do pinned versions affect cache warmup? If we switch versions, will the KV cache be invalidated?
[15:50] Priya: Yes, switching model binary invalidates KV caches; that will cause a temporary latency spike until caches warm. That's a reason to prefer variant-side fallback (quant vs non-quant of same base) where possible, because tokenization/kv layout is more compatible.
[16:22] Jordan: Good point—so fallback inside same family minimizes cache churn.
[16:40] Morgan: For canary traffic percentage, what's a safe starting point?
[16:52] Priya: Start 2-5% for 24-48 hours with active monitoring. Then bump to 10% if stable for a day. Also set auto-rollback if regressions breach thresholds.
[17:15] Alex: Action item—Priya to prepare an automated policy template for rollback thresholds we can drop into your console.
[17:30] Priya: I'll attach that policy to the follow-up email.
[18:05] Elena: A question on compatibility—does Redwood console show per-token cost broken down by model variant?
[18:22] Alex: Yes, console shows token-level cost and latency by route/model. We'll share a route-level breakdown for your pilot route.
[18:40] Morgan: On the topic of rollbacks, what's the worst-case time to switch traffic away in an outage?
[18:55] Diego: If traffic is controlled via policy, switch is near-instant for new requests; existing pinned sessions have to drain. In practice, full mitigation across sessions can take up to a few minutes depending on session length.
[19:20] Jordan: That's acceptable if we do canary small. But we also want an emergency stop that returns 100% to a cheap fallback—how fast is that?
[19:35] Priya: Emergency stop with forced reroute is immediate for new requests; we can force immediate replacement for new sessions. Existing sessions may still incur tokens while they drain.
[19:55] Samir: Regarding audit logs—can you give us a redacted sample that includes model_version, request_id, timestamp, user_id? We need to show the format to our compliance team.
[20:10] Alex: Yes, I'll attach a sample log in the follow-up.
[20:30] Morgan: Anything open on quality? Elena — did the regression tests show any edge-cases we should worry about?
[20:42] Elena: A couple of prompt types (table extraction and nested bullet lists) had lower fidelity on q4. Not catastrophic but measurable at the unit-test level—about a 6% drop in exact-match on our test set. So if we put q4 as fallback we need post-deploy monitoring of those prompt types.
[21:12] Priya: Good flag. We'll add per-prompt-type monitors and surface them in dashboard.
[21:40] Alex: Ok summarizing so far: proto decision—primary Cedar-2 non-quant pinned, fallback Cedar-2 q4 if possible, else Orchid-1.3 as secondary fallback. Can we get consensus?
[22:05] Morgan: That sounds right — leaning to Cedar primary / q4 fallback. We just need the cost delta and the specific rollback thresholds.
[22:25] Jordan: Also want a plan for cache tuning if we hit eviction spikes—thresholds and telemetry to watch.
[22:40] Diego: We'll provide recommended cache settings and a script to toggle prefix trimming.
[23:00] Priya: On the canary duration and targets: let's define success as no p95 latency regression > 20% and no quality regression > 5% on prompt sets for 48 hours at 5% traffic.
[23:30] Elena: Agree. We'll feed our metrics into the webhook and correlate.
[24:00] Morgan: For stakeholders, I'll loop in legal for export controls and Samir for compliance sign-off.
[24:20] Samir: Thanks. One more ask—do you support creating a signed attestation that model variants have not accessed customer data? We need that for procurement.
[24:40] Alex: We can provide an operations statement describing isolation guarantees for Dedicated and how hosted is handled; for Private we have more explicit attestations. I'll send a template.
[25:10] [brief cross-talk and laughter about onboarding docs]
[26:00] Priya: Quick demo note—when you do the canary we'll show you the live console with per-route token breakdown and the automated rollback button.
[26:20] Morgan: Sounds good.
[26:40] Alex: Finalizing next steps: Redwood to share perf/cost spreadsheet, policy template, sample audit log; Customer to provide prompt sets and confirm primary/fallback by next Tuesday. Also schedule rollback drill 2025-04-23.
[27:10] Elena: We'll deliver prompt sets and include representative long-chat transcripts for KV cache tests.
[27:40] Jordan: Also, we'll coordinate network and KMS folks for drill.
[28:00] Alex: Great. Any other questions?
[28:12] Morgan: One question—if we hit a regression during canary, what's the communication plan?
[28:30] Alex: We'll open a dedicated incident channel, Redwood AE and SE join, immediate rollback if thresholds exceeded, SRE runbook invoked. We'll share runbook excerpt as part of follow-up.
[29:00] Samir: Can we also require a signed change approval for switching primary models during pilot?
[29:20] Morgan: That makes sense—I'll add an approval gate for production rollouts.
[29:40] Alex: Noted.
[30:00] [audio notch where a sentence drops out]
[31:05] Priya: Quick technical caveat—pinning to an immutable model version can affect latency if that version is older and not compiled with the latest kernels; we'll call out performance delta per version in the spreadsheet.
[31:40] Elena: Good to see that—please highlight kernel/compile flags in the sheet.
[32:05] Alex: We'll annotate.
[32:40] Morgan: If everything looks ok after canary, what's the recommended next step to ramp?
[32:55] Priya: Gradual ramp 5% -> 25% -> 50% over a week with progressive checks. Alternatively you can commit to Dedicated for steady throughput but that's a procurement decision.
[33:20] Morgan: We'll keep it staged.
[33:40] Diego: One more note—when you pin a model, backups of the model binary are kept for 90 days in the catalog unless you request longer retention. That matters for rollback provenance.
[34:00] Samir: Please document retention policy and provide an export for our audit.
[34:20] Alex: We'll include retention details.
[34:50] Morgan: Ok I think that's everything. Let's recap next steps and owners.
[35:05] Alex: Recap—Priya: KV-cache stress test and policy template; Alex: perf/cost sheet and sample logs; Diego: cache tuning script; Elena: prompt sets; Morgan: confirm pinned models by Tues.
[35:35] Morgan: We should also include a timeline for the canary start date once we get the sheet.
[35:50] Alex: We'll propose dates in the follow-up email.
[36:10] [closing pleasantries]
[36:30] Alex: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with artifacts and calendar invites.
[36:45] Morgan: Thanks all.
[47:00] End of recording.
